requirements.summary: Reset takes effect on rising clock edges. Hold reset for at least one complete cycle. Master CYC and STB are inactive during reset; other master payload values are unspecified.
CYC qualifies bus activity and spans a transfer cycle. Without CYC, slave request signals are inactive. System reset remains effective.

Pipelined acceptance requires CYC and STB high and STALL low. WE distinguishes writes from reads. New requests need not wait for earlier acknowledgments. ACK can occur while STB is low. Successful transactions retire with acknowledgments; read data is meaningful with ACK.
ERR reports failure; the base protocol leaves the master reaction unspecified. ACK, ERR and RTY cannot coincide. Payload belongs to a strobed request. This interface has no RTY signal.

requirements.location: What is a Crossbar?; Returning data, paragraphs on nonexistent addresses and abort
requirements.summary: A crossbar connects masters to slaves without mixing their responses. A request outside every configured address range should return an error. A master may end its cycle to abort outstanding work; completed data must not later be attributed to a new transaction. The article motivates aborting a cycle after an error. Exact buffering, arbitration and timeout edge counts require explicit documentation rather than assumptions.

interface.packing: Port 0 occupies the least-significant slice. Each address is an 8-bit bus address, each data value 32 bits, each select 4 bits. No implicit byte-address shifting.
interface.address_configuration: Slave0: (addr & 0xf0)==0x00; slave1: (addr & 0xf0)==0x10. Other addresses match neither slave. This is public parameter decoding, not stimulus guidance.
interface.directions: i_m* are external master inputs; o_m* are DUT responses. o_s* are DUT requests to external slaves; i_s* are external slave responses. i_clk is the common clock.
interface.rows: [{cycle:int, pre:{all listed inputs and outputs}, post:{all listed outputs}}]; integers of declared width. None may represent undefined inactive payload, never a valid active control/data value.
interface.sampling: Inputs change while clock low. Pre sampled at +4ns, rising edge at +5ns, post at +9ns, falling edge at +10ns. One row is one physical cycle. Initial trace has two reset cycles followed by quiescence. No extra hidden clock edges.
interface.boundary: Checker consumes actual public-pin observations, not model offers or driver queue ledgers. Drivers may queue offers and hold pins through acceptance. Do not trust driver internal accounting as functional truth.
interface.environment_contract: External masters obey pipelined acceptance, holding pending request payload through backpressure except explicit cycle abort/reset. External slaves respond in acceptance order, may wait, and do not generate unsolicited responses. Slave work is canceled on cycle withdrawal/reset. Record violations separately from DUT faults. Exact future JSON offer fields are irrelevant to the pin-based checker.

Chapter 3. WISHBONE Classic Bus Cycles
WISHBONE Classic bus cycles are described in terms of their general operation, reset
operation, handshaking protocol and the data organization during transfers. Additional
requirements for bus cycles (especially those relating to the common clock) can be found in
the timing specifications in Chapter 5.
3.1     General Operation
MASTER and SLAVE interfaces are interconnected with a set of signals that permit them
to exchange data. For descriptive purposes these signals are cumulatively known as a bus,
and are contained within a functional module called the INTERCON. Address, data and
other information is impressed upon this bus in the form of bus cycles.

3.1.1     Reset Operation
All hardware interfaces are initialized to a pre-defined state. This is accomplished with the
reset signal [RST_O] that can be asserted at any time. It is also used for test simulation
purposes by initializing all self-starting state machines and counters which may be used in
the design. The reset signal [RST_O] is driven by the SYSCON module. It is connected to
the [RST_I] signal on all MASTER and SLAVE interfaces. Illustration 3-1: Reset cycle
shows the reset cycle.


                                                              NOTE(2)
                                  CLK_I           0                1    NOTE(1)    2                3




                 MASTER SIGNALS
                                  RST_I
                                                                                                  NOTE(3)
                                  STB_O


                                  CYC_O

                                          NOTES:
                                          (1) Reset cycles can be extended for any length of time.
                                          (2) Self-starting state machines & counters reset themselves at
                                              the rising [CLK_I] edge following the assertion of [RST_I].
                                              On MASTERs,[STB_O] and [CYC_O] are negated at the same time.
                                          (3) On MASTERs, [STB_O] and [CYC_O] may be asserted at the
                                              rising [CLK_I] edge following the negation of [RST_I].

                                              Illustration 3-1: Reset cycle

   RULE 3.00
All WISHBONE interfaces MUST initialize themselves at the rising [CLK_I] edge following
the assertion of [RST_I]. They MUST stay in the initialized state until the rising [CLK_I]
edge that follows the negation of [RST_I].

   RULE 3.05
[RST_I] MUST be asserted for at least one complete clock cycle on all WISHBONE
interfaces.

   PERMISSION 3.00
[RST_I] MAY be asserted for more than one clock cycle, and MAY be asserted indefinitely.


     Back to TOC                                Copyright © 2010 OpenCores                                   Page 31 / 128

Wishbone B4


   RULE 3.10
All WISHBONE interfaces MUST be capable of reacting to [RST_I] at any time.

   RULE 3.15
All self-starting state machines and counters in WISHBONE interfaces MUST initialize
themselves at the rising [CLK_I] edge following the assertion of [RST_I]. They MUST stay
in the initialized state until the rising [CLK_I] edge that follows the negation of [RST_I].

   OBSERVATION 3.00
In general, self-starting state machines do not need to be initialized. However, this may
cause problems because some simulators may not be sophisticated enough to find an initial
starting point for the state machine. Furthermore, self-starting state machines can go
through an indeterminate number of initialization cycles before finding their starting state,
thereby making it difficult to predict their behavior at start-up time. The initialization rule
prevents both problems by forcing all state machines to a pre-defined state in response to
the assertion of [RST_I].

   RULE 3.20
The following MASTER signals MUST be negated at the rising [CLK_I] edge following the
assertion of [RST_I], and MUST stay in the negated state until the rising [CLK_I] edge
that follows the negation of [RST_I]: [STB_O], [CYC_O]. The state of all other MASTER
signals are undefined in response to a reset cycle.

   OBSERVATION 3.05
On MASTER interfaces [STB_O] and [CYC_O] may be asserted beginning at the rising
[CLK_I] edge following the negation of [RST_I].


   OBSERVATION 3.10
SLAVE interfaces automatically negate [ACK_O], [ERR_O] and [RTY_O] when their
[STB_I] is negated in standard mode.
In pipelined mode the assertion of [ACK_O], [ERR_O] and [RTY_O] is done
independently of [STB_I].

   RECOMENDATION 3.00
Design SYSCON modules so that they assert [RST_O] during a power-up condition.
[RST_O] should remain asserted until all voltage levels and clock frequencies in the system
are stabilized. When negating [RST_O], do so in a synchronous manner that conforms to
this specification.

   OBSERVATION 3.15
If a gated clock generator is used, and if the clock is stopped, then the WISHBONE
interface is not capable of responding to its [RST_I] signal.

   SUGGESTION 3.00
Some circuits require an asynchronous reset capability. If an IP core or other SoC
component requires an asynchronous reset, then define it as a non-WISHBONE signal.
This prevents confusion with the WISHBONE reset [RST_I] signal that uses a purely
synchronous protocol, and needs to be applied to the WISHBONE interface only.


     Back to TOC               Copyright © 2010 OpenCores                Page 32 / 128

Wishbone B4


   OBSERVATION 3.20
All WISHBONE interfaces respond to the reset signal. However, the IP Core connected to
a WISHBONE interface does not necessarily need to respond to the reset signal.

3.1.2     Transfer Cycle initiation
MASTER interfaces initiate a transfer cycle by asserting [CYC_O]. When [CYC_O] is
negated, all other MASTER signals are invalid.
SLAVE interfaces respond to other SLAVE signals only when [CYC_I] is asserted.
SYSCON signals and responses to SYSCON signals are not affected.

   RULE 3.25
MASTER interfaces MUST assert [CYC_O] for the duration of SINGLE READ / WRITE,
BLOCK and RMW cycles. [CYC_O] MUST be asserted no later than the rising [CLK_I]
edge that qualifies the assertion of [STB_O]. [CYC_O] MUST be negated no earlier than
the rising [CLK_I] edge that qualifies the negation of [STB_O].

   PERMISSION 3.05
MASTER interfaces MAY assert [CYC_O] indefinitely.

   RECOMMENDATION 3.05
Arbitration logic often uses [CYC_I] to select between MASTER interfaces. Keeping
[CYC_O] asserted may lead to arbitration problems. It is therefore recommended that
[CYC_O] is not indefinitely asserted.

   RULE 3.30
SLAVE interfaces MAY NOT respond to any SLAVE signals when [CYC_I] is negated.
However, SLAVE interfaces MUST always respond to SYSCON signals.

3.1.3     Handshaking Protocol
All bus cycles use a handshaking protocol between the MASTER and SLAVE interfaces.
There exists two different traffic modes, standard and pipelined.

3.1.3.1   Standard wishbone protocol

As shown in Figure 3-2, the MASTER asserts [STB_O] when it is ready to transfer data.
[STB_O] remains asserted until the SLAVE asserts one of the cycle terminating signals
[ACK_I], [ERR_I] or [RTY_I]. At every rising edge of [CLK_I] the terminating signal is
sampled. If it is asserted, then [STB_O] is negated. This gives both MASTER and SLAVE
interfaces the possibility to control the rate at which data is transferred.




        Illustration 3-2: Standard bus handshaking protocol, asynchronous slave.



     Back to TOC              Copyright © 2010 OpenCores            Page 33 / 128

Wishbone B4




      Illustration 3-3: Standard wishbone handshaking protocol, synchronous slave.



   PERMISSION 3.10
If in standard mode the SLAVE guarantees it can keep pace with all MASTER interfaces
and if the [ERR_I] and [RTY_I] signals are not used, then the SLAVE’s [ACK_O] signal
MAY be tied to the logical AND of the SLAVE’s [STB_I] and [CYC_I] inputs. The interface
will function normally under these circumstances.

   OBSERVATION 3.25
In standard mode SLAVE interfaces assert a cycle termination signal in response to
[STB_I]. However, [STB_I] is only valid when [CYC_I] is valid.

   RULE 3.35
In standard mode the cycle termination signals [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and [RTY_O] must be
generated in response to the logical AND of [CYC_I] and [STB_I].

   PERMISSION 3.15
Other signals, besides [CYC_I] and [STB_I], MAY be included in the generation of the
cycle termination signals.

   OBSERVATION 3.30
Internal SLAVE signals also determine what cycle termination signal is asserted and when
it is asserted.
Most of the examples in this specification describe the use of [ACK_I] to terminate a local
bus cycle. However, the SLAVE can optionally terminate the cycle with an error [ERR_O],
or request that the cycle be retried [RTY_O].
All MASTER interfaces include the [ACK_I] terminator signal. Asserting this signal during
a bus cycle causes it to terminate normally.
Asserting the [ERR_I] signal during a bus cycle will terminate the cycle. It also serves to
notify the MASTER that an error occurred during the cycle. This signal is generally used if
an error was detected by SLAVE logic circuitry. For example, if the SLAVE is a parity-
protected memory, then the [ERR_I] signal can be asserted if a parity fault is detected.
This specification does not dictate what the MASTER will do in response to [ERR_I].
Asserting the optional [RTY_I] signal during a bus cycle will terminate the cycle. It also
serves to notify the MASTER that the current cycle should be aborted, and retried at a later
time. This signal is generally used for shared memory and bus bridges. In these cases
SLAVE circuitry asserts [RTY_I] if the local resource is busy. This specification does not
dictate when or how the MASTER will respond to [RTY_I].

   RULE 3.40
As a minimum, the MASTER interface MUST include the following signals: [ACK_I],


     Back to TOC               Copyright © 2010 OpenCores              Page 34 / 128

Wishbone B4


[CLK_I], [CYC_O], [RST_I], and [STB_O]. As a minimum, the SLAVE interface MUST
include the following signals: [ACK_O], [CLK_I], [CYC_I], [STB_I], and [RST_I]. All
other signals are optional.

   PERMISSION 3.20
MASTER and SLAVE interfaces MAY be designed to support the [ERR_I] and [ERR_O]
signals. In these cases, the SLAVE asserts [ERR_O] to indicate that an error has occurred
during the bus cycle. This specification does not dictate what the MASTER does in
response to [ERR_I].

   PERMISSION 3.25
MASTER and SLAVE interfaces MAY be designed to support the [RTY_I] and [RTY_O]
signals. In these cases, the SLAVE asserts [RTY_O] to indicate that the interface is busy,
and that the bus cycle should be retried at a later time. This specification does not dictate
what the MASTER will do in response to [RTY_I].

   RULE 3.45
If a SLAVE supports the [ERR_O] or [RTY_O] signals, then the SLAVE MUST NOT assert
more than one of the following signals at any time: [ACK_O], [ERR_O] or [RTY_O].

   OBSERVATION 3.35
If the SLAVE supports the [ERR_O] or [RTY_O] signals, but the MASTER does not
support these signals, deadlock may occur.

   RECOMMENDATION 3.10
Design INTERCON modules to prevent deadlock conditions. One solution to this problem
is to include a watchdog timer function that monitors the MASTER’s [STB_O] signal, and
asserts [ERR_I] or [RTY_I] if the cycle exceeds some pre-defined time limit. INTERCON
modules can also be designed to disconnect interfaces from the WISHBONE bus if they
constantly generate bus errors and/or watchdog time-outs.

   RECOMMENDATION 3.15
Design WISHBONE MASTER interfaces so that there are no intermediate logic gates
between a registered flip-flop and the signal outputs on [STB_O] and [CYC_O]. Delay
timing for [STB_O] and [CYC_O] are very often the most critical paths in the system. This
prevents sloppy design practices from slowing down the interconnect because of added
delays on these two signals.

   RULE 3.50
SLAVE interfaces MUST be designed so that the [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and [RTY_O] signals
are asserted and negated in response to the assertion and negation of [STB_I].

   PERMISSION 3.30
The assertion of [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and [RTY_O] MAY be asynchronous to the [CLK_I]
signal (i.e. there is a combinatorial logic path between [STB_I] and [ACK_O]).

   OBSERVATION 3.40
The asynchronous assertion of [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and [RTY_O] assures that the
interface can accomplish one data transfer per clock cycle. Furthermore, it simplifies the
design of arbiters in multi-MASTER applications.

     Back to TOC               Copyright © 2010 OpenCores                Page 35 / 128

Wishbone B4


   OBSERVATION 3.45
The asynchronous assertion of [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and [RTY_O] could proof impossible
to implement. For example slave wait states are easiest implemented using a registered
[ACK_O] signal.

   OBSERVATION 3.50
In large high speed designs the asynchronous assertion of [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and
[RTY_O] could lead to unacceptable delay times, caused by the loopback delay from the
MASTER to the SLAVE and back to the MASTER. Using registered [ACK_O], [ERR_O],
and [RTY_O] signals significantly reduces this loopback delay, at the cost of one additional
wait state per transfer. See WISHBONE Registered Feedback Bus Cycles for methods of
eliminating the wait state.

   PERMISSION 3.35
Under certain circumstances SLAVE interfaces MAY be designed to hold [ACK_O] in the
asserted state. This situation occurs on point-to-point interfaces where there is a single
SLAVE on the interface, and that SLAVE always operates without wait states.

   RULE 3.55
MASTER interfaces MUST be designed to operate normally when the SLAVE interface
holds [ACK_I] in the asserted state.

3.1.3.2     Pipelined wishbone protocol

In pipelined mode the handshake protocol is somewhat different.
   ●    The master doesn't wait for [ACK_I] before outputting next address/data word on
        the bus
   ●    we have a [STALL_I] input in the master, indicating that the slave pipeline can
        accept another request at the moment. For a bus arbiter a multiplexer should be
        used to select the targeted slave [STALL_O] signal and feed that to the master. This
        path should be non registered.
   ●    master outputs the requests as long as [STALL_I] is low. When [STALL_I] is
        asserted, it waits. Also, the pipeline in the interconnect doesn't push any requests
        when [STALL_I] is asserted.
   ●    cycle consisting of N transactions is terminated with a sequence of N [ACK_I].
        Subsequent [ACK_I] indicate the finished transactions. Master terminates the bus
        cycle (by deasserting [CYC_O]) after receiving the last [ACK_I] pulse.
   ●    read data is valid when [ACK_I] is high.




       Back to TOC              Copyright © 2010 OpenCores               Page 36 / 128

Wishbone B4




                       Illustration 3-4: Pipelined mode, single access



   RULE 3.57
In pipelined mode a read transaction is started when the following signals are asserted
       [CYC_I], [STB_I]
and the following negated
       [STALL_I], [WE_I].

   RULE 3.58
In pipelined mode a write transaction is started when the following signals are asserted
       [CYC_I], [STB_I], [WE_I]
and the following negated
       [STALL_I].

   RULE 3.59
In pipelined mode the MASTER must accept [ACK_I] signals at any time after a
transaction is initiated.

3.1.4     Use of [STB_O]

   RULE 3.60
MASTER interfaces MUST qualify the following signals with [STB_O]: [ADR_O],
[DAT_O()], [SEL_O()], [WE_O], and [TAGN_O].

   PERMISSION 3.40
If a MASTER doesn’t generate wait states, then [STB_O] and [CYC_O] MAY be assigned
the same signal.

   OBSERVATION 3.55
[CYC_O] needs to be asserted during the entire transfer cycle. A MASTER that doesn’t
generate wait states doesn’t negate [STB_O] during a transfer cycle, i.e. it is asserted the
entire transfer cycle. Therefore it is allowed to use the same signal for [CYC_O] and
[STB_O]. Both signals must be present on the interface though.




     Back to TOC               Copyright © 2010 OpenCores                Page 37 / 128

supplementary_abort_prose.locations: discussion of bus abort; Returning data
supplementary_abort_prose.authority_level: Older explanatory article, not a version-specific cancellation timing contract
supplementary_abort_prose.paraphrase: The author describes dropping CYC after an error to abort outstanding work; pending transactions have uncertain status. Slave-side cycle withdrawal follows upstream abort. No further response should be attributed to the aborted master cycle. The prose does not specify which buffered requests survive partial propagation or a fixed bound on observing residual forwarding. Code examples are excluded from this specification-only packet.

observables: post.o_scyc and post.o_sstb in every row with pre.i_reset=1
pre.i_mcyc and pre.i_mstb in every reset row that follows a reset row

acceptance.dut_violation: post o_scyc!=0 or post o_sstb!=0 in any row with pre.i_reset=1.
env_violation: Master CYC/STB high in a reset row whose previous row was also a reset row (rule 3.20).
A reset pulse that is shorter than rule 3.05 requires.
acceptance.reset_row_events: In a reset row, no acceptance or response is recorded. Rule 3.00: interfaces initialize at that edge.
end_of_row: Discard all live entries, orphans, canceled identities and hypotheses.
Cumulative unresolved records persist for the batch.
acceptance.first_non_reset_row: A slave acceptance in the first non-reset row must match work accepted after the reset (R11). Post of the reset row is judged by the post check above.

clause_matrix.exclusions: DUT o_mack/o_merr inside reset rows are not judged beyond K13 and rule 3.45.

acceptance.write_identity: (WE=1, addr, SEL, data restricted to SEL-enabled byte lanes). SEL=0 compares no data lanes.
multiplicity: Each row with STB high and STALL low is one request, even if its payload equals the previous row's.
A request held through stall is counted once, at the row of acceptance.
Per row: at most one acceptance per master port and one per slave port.
acceptance.undefined_payload: The None check covers only the K2 identity projection of an accepted or held strobed request. That projection is WE, address and SEL, plus SEL-enabled data lanes when WE=1. None in the projection is an env violation on a master port and a DUT violation on a slave port. Read data lanes and SEL-disabled write lanes carry no identity and are never judged (rule 3.60 qualifies payload, but does not make non-identity lanes meaningful).

acceptance: A slave acceptance on port s requires decode(addr)==s.
An unmapped address (decode none) must never be forwarded.

acceptance.consumption: Each slave acceptance consumes exactly one identity-equal candidate. Eligible candidates are a live unforwarded entry of any master (accepted in this or an earlier row of the reset epoch), or a canceled-pool member.
acceptance.consumption_limit: Each candidate is consumed at most once.
acceptance.failure: If no candidate exists in a hypothesis, that hypothesis dies.
acceptance.association_free_projection: For every identity X: count(slave acceptances of X) <= count(master acceptances of X) in the reset epoch.

clause_matrix.acceptance: NOT judged: neither forward order nor side-effect order, within one slave or across slaves. Every scoped_pass report must list K5 as an explicit exclusion. A pass never asserts order preservation. This applies in particular to fault/live_order_swap and new_aba/younger_equal_first.

clause_matrix.source: README 188-196 ('ACK responses won't get crossed'); WB B4 3.1.3.2 ('N ACKs for N transactions', no tag)

acceptance.retirement: A master response in row c retires that master's oldest live entry accepted in a row < c.
acceptance.no_entry: Held-request condition HR(m,c) holds in either of two cases. (i) Held: row c has pre i_mcyc[m]&i_mstb[m]&o_mstall[m]. (ii) Acceptance edge: row c has a master acceptance on m, and row c-1 had m held under o_mstall with an identical K2 projection. An ERR (never an ACK) on m in row c with HR(m,c) branches; no branch is preferred. Branch A (ordinary): retire m's oldest live entry from rows < c under the K8 tags. If no such entry exists, branch A dies. Branch B (possible_starvation_err, unknown): retire nothing and keep every live entry. In case (ii), branch B splits further. B1 leaves the row-c entry live. B2 removes the row-c entry from the retirable FIFO, makes it a canceled-pool member tagged starvation_attributed (a later forward of it is tagged like post_abort_forward), and creates no pending obligation for it. Basis: wbxbar.v header 37-39 says a starved master gets a bus error, but states no phase, timing or precedence against outstanding retirements. The tag never claims starvation occurred and carries no latency inference. Withdrawal edge: if pre i_mcyc[m]=0 in row c after a held request in row c-1, K13 already records same_edge_response_after_abort (unresolved) and retires nothing, so no extra rule is needed. Without HR(m,c), a response with no retirable entry is invented and the hypothesis dies. An ACK never uses branch B: an ACK with no entry is invented (K6, inferred) in every case. Earlier deaths and violations are unaffected.
acceptance.non_retirable: Canceled and orphan entries are never retirable.

clause_matrix.source: WB B4 obs 3.10; 3.1.3.2 ('read data valid with ACK'); README
clause_matrix.status: normative for data validity; inferred for end-to-end preservation
acceptance: A master ACK in row c requires the retired entry to be forwarded and bound to a slave ACK in a row <= c, in the same hypothesis.
A same-row slave-to-master path is allowed (permission 3.30).
For a read, the full 32-bit o_mdata must equal that slave ACK's i_sdata slice.

clause_matrix.source: WB B4 perm 3.20, rule 3.45; crossbar article (unmapped -> ERR); wbxbar.v header 32-39 (timeout/starvation)
clause_matrix.status: normative: exclusivity; inferred: decode ERR and slave-ERR propagation; unknown: timeout/starvation conditions and precedence, including ERR on an unaccepted held request (possible_starvation_err, see K6)
acceptance: A master ACK retiring an unmapped entry kills the hypothesis.
A master ACK retiring a slave-ERRed entry kills the hypothesis.
ERR retiring an unmapped or slave-ERRed entry is consistent.

ERR retiring a mapped entry that has no slave ERR is tagged unexplained_mapped_err (unknown). This covers unforwarded entries, entries forwarded but not yet answered, and entries already slave-ACKed. Timeout precedence against a slave ACK is undocumented, so no unconditional no-ERR rule applies.

acceptance: o_mack/o_merr[m] in row c with pre i_mcyc[m]=0 in both rows c-1 and c is a dut_violation (inferred, K13). No DUT response latency is derived from OPT_DBLBUFFER or any other option name; the one-row allowance follows only from the same-edge observability argument below. A response with CYC low is not an active-cycle retirement, so K6 is not cited as an independent basis for it.

ownership_algorithm.model: Exact-history nondeterministic reference. The first implementation has no symmetry quotient and no partitioning (both withdrawn per R2/R3). State is a set H of explicit hypotheses for the current reset epoch.
hypothesis_state: Per master: FIFO of live entries.
Each entry carries: identity, accept_row, master_epoch, reset_epoch.
Entry state is one of: unforwarded, forwarded(s,k), slave_acked(data,row), slave_erred(row), slave_canceled.
Canceled pool: a list of distinct member records, not merged even when equal.
Per slave: FIFO of forward records bound to a live entry ref, canceled member ref, or orphan.
ownership_algorithm.counters: master_epoch[m] increments on every CYC 1->0, and reset_epoch increments per reset. The association-free projection counters are also arbitrary-precision in the checker: per-identity master and slave counts, per-slave forwards and responses, and per-master acceptances and responses in the current CYC. None of them is ever pruned or truncated when hypothesis resources are exhausted, so the projections stay exact and sound. If a bounded implementation is used and any counter would overflow, that counter's projection becomes unresolved_on_counter_limit(row) for the rest of the reset epoch. It never wraps or saturates into a verdict.
row_order: 0 Reset row: apply K1 and stop processing the row.
1 CYC drop: for each m with pre i_mcyc[m]=0, apply K9 transitions. If 1->0, increment master_epoch[m].
2 Master acceptances: append new live entries (accept_row=c).
3 Slave CYC: for each s with pre o_scyc[s]=0, mark all FIFO-s forwards slave_canceled and empty the FIFO.
4 Slave responses: apply K11 env checks, then bind each to its FIFO-s head among forwards from rows < c.
5 Slave acceptances: branch over every identity-equal candidate (live unforwarded from rows <= c, or canceled member), and append to FIFO s.
6 Master responses: apply K13, then K6/K7/K8 retirement against entries from rows < c, using slave responses from rows <= c.
7 Association-free checks: K3, K10 and env hold, independent of H.
same_edge_dependencies: Slave response row c can retire only forwards from rows < c.
A forward in row c may consume a master acceptance from row c. This is permissive and adds branches only.
A master response in row c may use a slave response from row c, but never a master acceptance from row c.
A forward in the same row as a CYC drop is tagged post_abort_forward.

verdict_semantics.trace_membership: Exists a surviving hypothesis. If H becomes empty, the result is dut_violation. Cite the dying row, the per-branch witnesses and every inferred clause that was used.
verdict_semantics.clause_level: With H nonempty, a judged clause is pass only if no surviving hypothesis carries ANY tag of class unknown, and none has pending work. The tag class is generic. Current members are post_abort_forward, unexplained_mapped_err, same_edge_response_after_abort, possible_starvation_err, starvation_attributed and unresolved_owner_alternative. Any future tag defaults to class unknown unless the design explicitly classifies it otherwise. Failing that test, the clause is unresolved(clause), listing the alternatives and their downstream consequences.
verdict_semantics.aggregate_precedence: Time-bounded. Let e be the first row with an env violation. (1) A DUT violation whose complete evidence lies in rows < e stays dut_violation; a later invalid input cannot erase it. (2) A DUT violation evidenced in row e itself, as a same-edge mixed fault, is reported as mixed_same_edge(dut_candidate, env) with the explicit note that no public ordering exists. It is unresolved for the DUT, unless the DUT check depends only on pins and on inputs from rows < e. (3) Every judgment needing rows >= e is input_or_scope_invalid. A clause whose evidence lies wholly before e may still be reported as prefix_scoped_pass, bounded to rows < e. (4) Trace aggregate: dut_violation if (1) applies, else input_or_scope_invalid if e exists, else violation > unresolved > pass. Both the env record and any prefix verdict are always listed.
verdict_semantics.ownership: unique-by-elimination only if all survivors agree; otherwise indistinguishable(k). Never a hidden-state claim.
non_circularity: A hypothesis is removed only when a specific observed pin value contradicts an independently cited clause applied to that branch's bindings.
A pass is therefore 'not refuted by the reference', a membership statement. It is not universal evidence that the DUT satisfies the clause on other traces, and not proof of internal ownership.
Universality is evaluated only over the unknown-tag and pending dimensions, never over clauses used for filtering.

resource_limits.constants: MAX_HYP=4096, MAX_LIVE_PER_MASTER=64, MAX_CANCELED_POOL=256. Declared, test-lowerable, never silently changed.
resource_limits.on_exhaustion: No pruning and no branch selection. For the remainder of the current reset epoch, record unresolved_on_limit(row, sizes) and suspend all association-dependent judgments for all masters: K4 per-candidate consumption, K6, K7, K8 attribution, K9 tags and K12. Violations recorded before the exhaustion row stay final. Mandatory metric for each run and each clause: suspended_rows, total_rows, the suspended fraction, and the exhaustion rows and sizes. A clause suspended in any row may never be reported scoped_pass; the best it can be is unresolved(suspended). The report also states the effective checked scope in rows.
still_valid_after_exhaustion: K4 association-free count projection per identity

Per-master ACKs in the current CYC <= acceptances in the current CYC. This holds regardless of ERR attribution. ERRs not meeting HR(m,c) are added to that bound: ACKs + non-HR ERRs <= acceptances. ERRs meeting HR(m,c) are counted separately, tagged unknown, and added to neither side, so the bound can neither falsely fail nor certify attribution. All counters are arbitrary-precision; a bounded counter that would overflow yields unresolved_on_counter_limit, never a wrap or saturation verdict.
resource_limits.resume: Only at reset. This removes the R4 contradiction: there is no mid-epoch closure.

A free ghost association variable therefore asserts over ALL associations, and a failing arbitrary association is not a DUT failure.
Membership is expressible only via a determinized monitor. That monitor is the H set, with explicit finite bounds as assumptions, and the claim is bounded.

findings.detail: One of 46 author selftests fails: mixed_same_edge_explicit. The offline gate is therefore false. Agreement on the 127+6 control cases cannot override this. Registration stays blocked until the test and the rule are reconciled and the whole suite passes.

The trace has three relevant facts. In row 3, master 0 changes a stalled payload, which is an env violation. Master 1 has CYC high and STB low and was never accepted. Master 1 then receives an ACK.

The K6 count bound for an ACK uses only rows < c acceptances and the DUT o_mack pin. An ACK never uses HR branch B. Master 1's own inputs are valid. So for an ACK the failure depends only on pins and inputs from rows < e, and rule (2) supports keeping dut_violation.

The old selftest expectation (input_or_scope_invalid) is therefore stale for the ACK case, and P4 is acceptable for ACKs.

ERRs are different. Classifying an ERR as non-HR depends on row-c held or accept conditions (o_mstall, STB and the projection in row c, plus the identity comparison with row c-1). These are row-e inputs. A K6 count failure caused by a non-HR ERR in row e must stay mixed_same_edge, unless the HR determination uses only master m's row-c pins and m is not the env-violating port. Even then this must be argued explicitly. The code currently keeps every K6_count_projection failure (pin=True), including ERR-driven ones. The fix is to make ERR-driven K6 count failures in row e non-pin.

The second unresolved entry is correctly mixed: the membership_empty_H item is association-dependent.

findings.detail:
In diagnostic/tag_then_mixed_same_edge, DUT judgment at row 19 is withheld as mixed_same_edge. Even so, discarded_epoch_evidence labels the possible_starvation_err@8 histories as 'refuted at cycle 19 by concrete pin contradiction'. That refutation is invalid: it rests on row-e evidence whose DUT judgment the contract withholds.

The tag also lies wholly in the valid prefix (row 8 < e), yet it is absent from unresolved. The prefix status is reported as prefix_unresolved without the item that makes it unresolved.

Required behaviour when the death happens at row e and is reclassified as mixed: do not record it as refuted. Flush the row-start tags as cumulative valid-prefix unknowns, using the tag_row and class unknown.

findings.area: P1 dying-row tags and exhaustion snapshot
findings.detail:
Omitting tags created in the dying row is acceptable for a genuine death, because every history died. It must be disclosed per event, not only in prose.

At exhaustion, exhaust() flushes the tags of S['H'] as they stand at call time. When it is called from the step-5 branching pre-check, that is the pre-expansion set. When it is called from exhaust_check after expansion, it is the post-expansion set. The report says 'feasible immediately before suspension' without stating which applies.

The report should state the snapshot point. It should also report the projected history count (the total) separately from the actual count.
The display totals, displayed and omitted counts are present and nothing is pruned. P3 is acceptable.

P5 decisions, assessed individually:
- B2 with an already-forwarded entry: acceptable, because B1 is always kept and the result is tagged unknown. focused/hr_acceptance_and_forward_same_row shows that only branch B survives, with a tag, and the verdict is unresolved.
- Hypothesis-dependent env classification of undefined i_sdata: should become association-free. Make undefined i_sdata on any slave ACK an env violation when that slave's FIFO head is a read forward in any history, and document this. Alternatively, keep the current rule but list it as an unresolved contract gap.
- Undefined DUT control output treated as a DUT violation that stops judgment: acceptable.
- K13 not judged on the first row: harmless, since the first row must be a reset row.

Proposed contract decisions must not be labelled normative.

properties.json K10 and VERDICT do not mention P4 (K6 count kept at row e). contract.md still lists F4 as a blocker while also stating P4. The hr_err_unjudged and activation fields are undocumented in properties.json.

contract_decision_assessments.detail: Pre-suspension flushing and per-epoch records are accepted. Refuted disclosure is accepted only for deaths wholly before e. A death at row e reclassified as mixed must flush its tags as open unknowns. The snapshot point must be stated.
Raw counters must be split into checked, suspended and post-death counts. Zero activation must never count as a pass or a cover claim.
ERR-driven K6 count failures at row e depend on row-e HR inputs and must be mixed_same_edge. The K4 projection stays mixed, as does membership death.
B2-forwarded, undefined DUT control output and first-row K13 are accepted as scoped decisions. The undefined i_sdata env rule should be made association-free or kept listed as an open gap.

required_followup: Change the K6 count failure to pin=False when the response is an ERR (or when the boundary row's HR classification is involved). Keep it pin=True for ACKs.

Update mixed_same_edge_explicit to expect dut_violation, plus a K6_count_projection failure and a mixed_same_edge unresolved entry for the ACK. Add a companion ERR case expecting input_or_scope_invalid with mixed_same_edge. The gate requires 46 or more of 46 passing.
In boundary(), when the membership death is reclassified as mixed, move its disc entries to unresolved as valid-prefix unknown tags. Do not label them refuted.
Add per-clause checked, suspended, post-death and unknown counts. State the exhaustion snapshot point and the projected count.
Sync contract.md and properties.json, remove the stale blocker text, then rerun all 144 traces and the selftests. Registration is still required. No freeze and no B/C.

def _row(c, **kw):
    pre = {}
    for k in KI + KO:
        pre[k] = 0
    post = {}
    for k in KO:
        post[k] = 0
    for k in kw:
        if k.startswith('post_'):
            post[k[5:]] = kw[k]
        else:
            pre[k] = kw[k]
    return {'cycle': c, 'pre': pre, 'post': post}


def _rst():
    return [_row(0, i_reset=1), _row(1, i_reset=1)]


def _shift(rows, off):
    return [{'cycle': r['cycle'] + off, 'pre': r['pre'], 'post': r['post']} for r in rows]

    r = _rst()
    r.append(_row(2, i_mcyc=1, i_mstb=1, i_mwe=1, i_maddr=0x05, i_mdata=0xAB, i_msel=sel))

# WBXBAR exact-history reference checker (candidate)

Scope: public pins of WBXBAR rev 2e8d3bc2, NM=2, NS=2, AW=8, DW=32, slave0 = (addr&0xf0)==0x00, slave1 = (addr&0xf0)==0x10. Rows are pre/post samples; only pre defines transfers, post is used for K1 reset outputs. Candidate only: independent controls, code review, freeze and replay are required before any B/C.

## Model
Exact explicit hypothesis set H per reset epoch; no quotient, partition, deduplication or pruning. Each hypothesis holds per-master FIFOs of live entries (identity, accept_row, master_epoch, reset_epoch, state unforwarded/forwarded/slave_acked/slave_erred/slave_canceled), a canceled pool of distinct members, orphans, per-slave forward FIFOs and a tag list. Row order: reset; CYC drop; master acceptances; slave CYC withdrawal; slave responses (bind to forwards from rows < c); slave acceptances (branch over every identity-equal candidate); master responses (K13, then K6/K7/K8 against entries from rows < c); association-free checks.

## Verdicts
scoped_pass, dut_violation, input_or_scope_invalid, unresolved only. Per-clause statuses are in counts.property_status (violated, suspended, unresolved, checked_not_refuted, prefix_checked_not_refuted, excluded_not_judged). scoped_pass means not refuted by the reference on this trace; it excludes K5 forward order and unproved characterization C1-C4, and is not proof of hidden ownership. Ownership per epoch is unique_by_elimination or indistinguishable(k) in counts.pending_alternatives.

Time-bounded precedence: e = first row with an environment violation; processing stops there. DUT violations before e stay final. At row e, pin-only DUT checks (K1, K2 slave payload, K3, K10, K13, rule 3.45) stay dut_violation; an ACK-driven K6 per-CYC count-bound failure also stays dut_violation, while an ERR-driven one (non-HR classification uses row-e inputs) becomes mixed_same_edge; association-dependent or row-e-input-dependent candidates (empty H, K4 per-identity count projection) become mixed_same_edge(dut_candidate, env), unresolved, with a note that no public ordering exists. counts.prefix_status gives prefix_scoped_pass / prefix_unresolved / prefix_dut_violation for rows < e.

## Unknown tags
post_abort_forward, unexplained_mapped_err, same_edge_response_after_abort, possible_starvation_err, starvation_attributed; any unclassified tag defaults to unknown. Tags carried by any surviving history are flushed to cumulative unresolved records at reset and batch end; reset never erases cumulative uncertainty.

Repeated HR ERRs during one held request are absorbed by branch B and are not judged; they stay unknown.

## Resource limits
Defaults MAX_HYP=4096, MAX_LIVE_PER_MASTER=64, MAX_CANCELED_POOL=256. The limits argument is for development selftests only and is validated; frozen callers pass rows only. On exhaustion: unresolved_on_limit(row, sizes), association clauses (K4 per-candidate, K6, K7, K8 attribution, K9 tags, K12) suspended for all masters until reset; still checked: K1, K2, K3, K10, K11, K13, rule 3.45, K4 per-identity count projection, per-slave response count, per-CYC ACK+non-HR-ERR bound. Counters are arbitrary-precision Python ints. counts.checked_scope reports suspended rows, fraction, exhaustion rows/sizes and effective checked rows.

## Declared exclusions
K5 order; C1-C4; liveness/latency/deadlines; payload while STB low, read-data lanes on requests, SEL-disabled lanes; write ACK data; reset-row master responses beyond K13/3.45; rule 3.05 sub-row reset length; formal F1-F8 unproved.

## Implementation decisions and blockers (not settled by the reviewed contract)
- B2 when the row-c entry was already forwarded in the same row: treated as orphan with post_abort_forward + starvation_attributed tags (scoped decision accepted by review; contract still silent, B1 always kept).
- Undefined i_sdata on a slave ACK is an env violation when the pin-derived per-slave forward FIFO head (WE sampled at slave acceptance) is a read, independent of hypotheses; this includes orphan/canceled reads, since rule 3.1.3.2 makes read data meaningful with ACK regardless of master attribution.
- Simultaneous o_mack&o_merr: rule 3.45 violation, response not attributed.
- K13 is not judged on the first trace row (no c-1).
- The K6 count bound uses acceptances from earlier rows of the current CYC (consistent with K6 retiring only rows < c).
- Master STB without CYC is not an acceptance and is not separately flagged.
- slave_canceled live entries at batch end are counted (non-obligation), not pending.
- A row with undefined DUT control output is a DUT violation and stops judgment (unjudgeable_row).
- Mixed same-edge pin-only vs association-dependent split as described above.

## Follow-up repair status (review R1-R8; not normative authority)
- P4 narrowed to ACK only; ERR-driven K6 count failures at row e are mixed_same_edge.
- A membership death at row e reclassified as mixed is not a refutation: tags of histories alive at the row start are flushed as open valid-prefix unknowns with original tag rows; discarded_epoch_evidence only holds deaths wholly before e.
- Exhaustion records disclose snapshot point and actual vs projected hypothesis count; death records disclose omitted dying-row tags per event.
- Scope accounting: counts.subobligation_activations and counts.clause_scope (units: K1 reset rows; K2 master held/accepted strobes and slave acceptances; K3 slave acceptances; K4 slave acceptances with defined projection, split count_projection vs candidate_consumption; K6 master responses with CYC high, split count_bound vs attribution; K7 master ACKs; K8 master responses; K9 CYC 1->0; K10 slave strobe rows and ACK&ERR rows; K12 batch end; K13 responses with CYC low). Raw activations are exposure, not coverage.
- Still open: K5, C1-C4, F1-F8, timeout/cancellation bounds, both_interfaces_pending, rule 3.05 sub-row reset.

## Proposed decisions for fresh independent review (not normative authority)
- P1 (F1): On exhaustion, tags of the histories feasible immediately before suspension are flushed to unresolved (class unknown, marked pre-suspension) and a pending_alternatives record with reason suspended_on_limit is emitted. On membership death, tags carried by histories alive at the start of the dying row are recorded in counts.discarded_epoch_evidence, explicitly as refuted-history disclosure: not open uncertainty, not a hidden-owner fact, never masking the fault; a membership_dead record is emitted. Tags created within the dying row itself are not captured (disclosed limitation).
- P2 (F2): Per-clause activation units in counts.clause_activations: K1 reset rows; K2 master held/accepted strobes plus slave acceptances; K3/K4 slave acceptances; K6/K8 master responses with CYC high; K7 master ACKs; K9 master CYC 1->0 transitions; K10 slave strobe rows plus ACK&ERR rows; K11 nonreset rows; K12 batch-end closure; K13 responses with CYC low. A non-violated, non-suspended, non-unresolved clause with zero activations reports not_activated. Zero activation is never a DUT violation and never a formal or cover claim.
- P3 (F3): Displays capped at 16 histories and 8 witnesses with explicit histories_total/displayed/omitted and witness shown/total/omitted; no history is pruned for reporting.
- P4 (F4): The K6 per-CYC count bound uses only DUT response pins and acceptances from rows < c within the current CYC (a CYC drop at row c routes the response to K13), so at row e it depends only on pins and inputs from rows < e and is kept as dut_violation under precedence rule (2). The K4 per-identity projection counts row-c master acceptances (permitted same-row forward), so at row e it remains mixed_same_edge. Membership death at row e remains mixed_same_edge.
- P5 (F5): B2 on an entry already forwarded in its acceptance row: kept as orphan with post_abort_forward + starvation_attributed tags; branch B1 is always also kept, so no verdict depends on B2 alone. Undefined i_sdata on a slave ACK: superseded by the association-free pin FIFO-head rule above (integer drivers cannot emit None). Undefined pre DUT control output: DUT violation, judgment stops (unjudgeable_row). First-row K13 not judged (no c-1). All remain scoped decisions pending review.
- Events list is always empty; no recovery event or ownership proof is invented.
- Identical histories are not merged, so exhaustion may occur earlier than with a quotient; this is reported, never pruned.
